# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🫱]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 ✊]

I need to figure out what Mute is trying to tell me through these gestures. Since Mute can't speak (only I and Blind can hear speech, but Mute can't produce speech at all), Mute is using gestures to communicate with me since I can see.

Let me think about this. Mute has the manual. Mute is sending me gestures - three pairs. This could be encoding information about which wire, or asking me something, or trying to establish a code.

Since I can't respond with gestures that Mute would see in a useful loop (wait, actually I *can* gesture to Mute, and Mute can see gestures since Mute isn't deaf-blind, just can't hear/speak/touch). Let me re-check: Mute "cannot speak or touch" - so Mute can hear and see. Good, so Mute received nothing from me yet, and I should acknowledge and describe what I see, since Mute needs my visual info combined with the manual, and Blind needs to act but can only hear speech (not see gestures).

I should relay my bomb observations via speech, since Blind can hear me, and Mute can also hear me (Mute isn't deaf). This lets Mute cross-reference with the manual, and Blind gets raw info too even if they can't fully use it yet.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. I see: display shows 0, light is off, plate has an engraving I cannot read the meaning of, wires are 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👆", "🤟"])
```

Mute is sending 🫵 which often means "you" - perhaps pointing at me, asking me to do something or confirm something. Since I have no reliable shared code established, and the risk is high (bomb!), I should keep providing clear factual speech to both Mute and Blind, and let Mute figure out from the manual what matters, then have Mute speak instructions to Blind directly (since Mute can't speak - wait, Mute cannot speak at all).

This is critical: Mute cannot speak. So Mute can NEVER give verbal instructions to Blind. Mute can only gesture, and Blind cannot see gestures. So Mute and Blind cannot communicate directly at all!

This means: I am the only bridge between Mute (manual) and Blind (hands). I hear nothing from Mute (I can't hear - wait, "Deaf: cannot hear" - right, I can't hear speech either). But Mute can't speak anyway.

So the only channel FROM Mute TO anyone is gestures, which ONLY I can see. So Mute can only reach me, and only via gestures.

I need to relay: I speak to Blind (and Mute, though Mute can already hear if speaking works... wait Mute canNOT hear? Let me check - Mute's cannot list is "speak, or touch the bomb" - hearing isn't restricted, so Mute CAN hear.

So: I speak (Blind and Mute hear me). Mute gestures (only I see). Blind can hear me and hear Mute... no wait Mute can't speak so Blind never hears from Mute directly.

So full picture: I must relay bomb visuals to Mute via gesture or speech (speech works, Mute hears). Mute must relay manual info to me via gesture (only path). Then I must relay that to Blind via speech.

I need to ask Mute specific yes/no questions via gesture, using single-symbol codes, since Mute can only respond in gesture too (which only I see) - but wait, does Mute gesture back in response to my gestures? Yes, Mute can gesture to me. Good - a two way gesture channel exists between me and Mute.

Let me establish a simple protocol: I'll assign meanings to gestures explicitly via speech won't work since gestures aren't heard... but I can SPEAK the meaning while gesturing simultaneously? No - speech and gesture are separate channels, but I can send both in the same turn combined conceptually if I describe in speech what my gesture will mean, but Mute needs to correlate gesture+meaning, and only I can see gestures... but Mute also sees gestures (Mute isn't blind). So if I speak AND gesture, Mute gets both the words and the gesture, letting me define a code!

```
speak(to="mute", text="I will now define a code with gestures. Gesture 👍 from me means yes. Gesture 👎 from me means no. Gesture ☝ from me means wire one. Gesture ✌ means wire two. Gesture 🤟 means wire three. Please use the same gestures back to me: 👍 for yes, 👎 for no, and use ☝ ✌ 🤟 to indicate wire one two or three when answering me. Also tell me: does the manual instruction depend on the plate engraving symbol? I will describe its shape if you gesture 👍.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```
